THE CORPUS EXISTS AND IT FAILS THE FLOOR. data/consensus/vietnamese.json was recorded 2026-08-30 with FOUR sources: The Infatuation, Time Out, Luxury London and the LSE Students Blog. Three mastheads and a university blog. ZERO tier D (video), ZERO tier E (community), ZERO tier A recorded.

SKILL.md: tiers D and E are NOT optional. This corpus has neither. It is four writers agreeing with each other - the exact failure the breakfast topic was rebuilt to fix.

  LSE recorded NINE names, of which 'March 5th' and 'Affordable lunch spots at and near LSE' are chrome, and 'Longdan' and 'Ly Trang Supermarket' are GROCERS, not restaurants. Real yield: five, and two of those are shops.

theScopeQuestion:
DO PHO-ONLY COUNTERS AND BANH-MI-ONLY SHOPS BELONG IN A RESTAURANT GUIDE? SETTLED: YES, ONE PAGE, IN THEIR OWN SECTIONS.

The evidence is in what the serious sources actually publish. Time Out's single Vietnamese guide is titled 'London's 20 Best Vietnamese Restaurants for Pho and Bánh Mì' - it puts all three in one list under one headline. The Infatuation's Vietnamese guide already carries Banh Mi Kêu Deli and Bánh, a bakery. Excluding the counters would mean excluding venues the topic's two strongest sources put at the centre of it.

BUT THEY ARE A DIFFERENT DECISION AND NEED A DIFFERENT SECTION. A reader buying a £7 sandwich at a hatch and a reader booking a table at Cây Tre are not choosing from the same list. Use SKILL.md section 5 (Quickest) plus the facet sections below; do not interleave a bakery with a dining room and call it a ranking.

DO NOT SPIN OUT SEPARATE PAGES. SKILL.md: one page, sectioned, never split by style - competing pages on the same intent both rank worse. Note however that `best banh mi london` and `best pho london` each return their OWN dedicated guides (Infatuation, SquareMeal, Vittles and London x London all publish a standalone banh mi list; Foodism, Secret London and Ideal Magazine publish standalone pho lists). That is real evidence of distinct intent. It is NOT yet a reason to split - the method's stated exception is Search Console showing the section drawing its own distinct query. Revisit after the guide has data.

GROCERS ARE NOT RESTAURANTS. LSE's record contributed Longdan and Ly Trang Supermarket. Vietnamese supermarkets are useful to a reader and belong in prose, never as ranked venues.
theKingslandRoadQuestion:
VERDICT: LIST INDIVIDUAL VENUES, NEVER ONE AREA ENTRY. And the honest answer to 'is it still the best' is NO, NOT ANY MORE - THE DENSITY IS STILL THERE, THE CONSENSUS PICKS HAVE MOVED OUT. Give it a short named section, three or four sentences, not a paragraph of nostalgia.

WHY NOT ONE AREA ENTRY. Every rule in SKILL.md points the same way: one canonical venue name as Restaurants v2 spells it, named traders only and never the hall itself. 'Kingsland Road' is not bookable, has no price band and no citation count. The strip holds Sông Quê, Viet Grill, Mien Tay, Tay Do, Green Papaya, BunBunBun and Bánh, and the sources disagree sharply about which of them is good - collapsing that into one entry destroys exactly the signal this guide exists to publish.

THE EVIDENCE THAT THE REPUTATION HAS OUTLIVED ITSELF, in the topic's own leading source. The Infatuation's Vietnamese guide opens by saying Kingsland Road, the pho mile, 'was the place to go' - past tense - and that these days you can find superb Vietnamese restaurants all over the city. That is the strongest source in the corpus explicitly retiring the strip's monopoly, and no competitor guide says it plainly.

It holds up against where the picks actually are:
  The Infatuation's 10: Eat Vietnam Bar-B-Grill (DEPTFORD), Hai Cafe (CLAPTON), Hoa Sen (DRURY LANE), Lai Rai (PECKHAM), Cô Thành, Bánh - only Sông Quê and Bánh are on the strip.
  The one judged award in the topic, Lai Rai's Bib Gourmand, went to PECKHAM.
  Thuy Hoang, a Vietnamese chef and MasterChef quarter-finalist, names FOUR rooms: Deptford, Drury Lane, Rotherhithe and one on Kingsland Road.
  Two separate sources point past the strip at Phở Thúy Tây, a plain room out by Rotherhithe/Surrey Quays, as beating it - The Picky Glutton reviewed it and Time Out lists it.

THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE, WHICH IS REAL AND MUST BE CARRIED. Vittles argues the best bánh mì in London is at Bánh, a bakery ON Kingsland Road that bakes its own bread - and Bánh is a RECENT opening, not a pho-mile veteran. So the honest finding is not 'the strip declined'. It is that the strip's twenty-year-old family cafés no longer top the lists while new operators on the same street do. That is more interesting than either simple story and it is the thing to write.

HOUSE RULE: this goes in the article as findings, never as a weakness line. No 'the sources could not agree' hedging.

facetAxis.note:
DISH, NOT REGION - and the SERP settles it. `best pho london` and `best banh mi london` each return a full page of dedicated guides from serious publishers (Foodism, Secret London and Ideal Magazine on phở; The Infatuation, SquareMeal, Vittles and London x London on bánh mì). NOBODY publishes a 'northern Vietnamese London' guide, and no reader searches for one. Region is what an expert knows; dish is what a reader types.

REGION IS STILL LOAD-BEARING - CARRY IT PER VENUE, NOT AS THE AXIS. It is the single most interesting thing the sources disagree about, and exactly one source has it: Thuy Hoang distinguishes Phở Thúy Tây's Northern Hanoi lineage from Sông Quê's Southern recipes, and argues that hoisin and Thai basil do not belong in Northern phở. That is a fact a reader can act on at the table - it explains why two bowls both called phở taste nothing alike. Put it in the phở section's prose and in each venue's entry. Do not build six thin regional sections on one source.

formatSection.title: Where you can bring your own wine
formatSection.note:
BYO AND CORKAGE. VERIFIED AS REAL 2026-09-07, from three independent sources, and it decides a visit in a way price alone does not - a BYO room turns a £30 dinner for two into a £30 dinner for two with a good bottle.

THE EVIDENCE:
  The Nudge (8 Aug 2024): Mien Tay 'is also BYOB, with a small corkage fee'.
  Secret London (22 Mar 2024): Miến Tây Fulham and Shoreditch 'accept BYO (charges apply)'.
  The Infatuation's Vietnamese guide intro remembers Kingsland Road as the place for 'summer rolls and BYOB good times' - i.e. BYO is bound up with the strip's identity, which ties this section to theKingslandRoadQuestion.

WHY THIS ONE AND NOT THE OTHERS. Cash-only was NOT confirmed anywhere in this pass - Secret London and The Nudge were both checked and neither mentions it, so do not print it on a hunch. No-bookings is real at the counters but is already covered by the booking summary SKILL.md requires near the top. Lunch-only rooms did not surface. BYO is the one that is both verified and decision-changing.

BEFORE PRINTING IT: VERIFY PER VENUE AT THE VENUE'S OWN SITE OR BY PHONE, and print the corkage figure where it is knowable. A listicle saying BYO is not evidence, corkage policies change, and a reader who arrives with a bottle and is charged £15 has been failed by this guide. Where it cannot be confirmed, leave the venue out of the section rather than guessing.
